title: GeoAI-Powered Wildfire Risk Assessment and Community Vulnerability Mapping
summary: This project develops explainable GeoAI models to assess wildfire risk and identify socially vulnerable communities in the western U.S. We integrate multi-source remote sensing, socioeconomic data, and physics-informed AI for near-real-time risk mapping.
objectives: Develop transformer-based models for wildfire progression prediction
Map community vulnerability using responsible AI principles
Create open-source tools for fire risk visualization and communication

title: Responsible AI for Flood Damage Assessment Using Multi-Temporal Satellite Imagery
summary: PLACEHOLDER: Project description. We develop deep learning models for automated flood damage assessment using Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery, with a focus on bias mitigation across different socioeconomic regions.

title: Coupled Nature-Human Risk Modeling: Hurricane Impacts on Coastal Communities
summary: PLACEHOLDER: Project description. This project investigates how coupled nature-human system dynamics influence hurricane impact severity, recovery trajectories, and adaptive capacity across Gulf Coast communities.

title: Spatial Fairness in GeoAI: Detecting and Mitigating Geographic Bias in AI Models
summary: PLACEHOLDER: Project description. This foundational research examines sources of geographic and demographic bias in GeoAI models and develops methodological frameworks for fairness-aware geospatial AI.

title: Urban Heat Island Detection and Environmental Justice Using Remote Sensing and GeoAI
summary: PLACEHOLDER: Project description. This project will map urban heat island patterns with high spatial resolution and analyze their unequal distribution across income and race demographics in major U.S. cities.

title: Multi-Hazard Risk Atlas for the Tennessee Valley Region
summary: PLACEHOLDER: Project description. We developed a comprehensive multi-hazard risk atlas integrating data on floods, tornadoes, severe storms, and drought for the Tennessee Valley region to support emergency management.
